o1.biggest_strength: Calls the in-app checkout bug first, sizes the money, and gives five ranked tests with honest MDEs and sensible metric choices.
o1.biggest_mistake: Tests 1 and 2 overlap and the interaction handling is loose; firmness is left as a review-move test rather than a direct firmness answer.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Add an explicit assumptions and A/A split-hygiene block, tighten the overlapping-test read or sequence them, and test a plain firmness explainer directly.

o2.biggest_strength: Excellent diagnostic table; ties the pop-up errors to the exact in-app checkout gap and gives a clear schedule, A/A check and tracking plan.
o2.biggest_mistake: Bundles hero image and review reordering into one test, so a win cannot be attributed; and uses orders rather than add-to-cart for the size test, making it slower and less sensitive.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Split the hero and review changes into separate tests, switch the size test to add-to-cart with orders as guardrail, and keep the clean schedule and A/A check.

reason: I would rather run Output 1: it is more rigorous on metric choice and sample-size maths and keeps the hero and review tests separate. Output 2 is very readable and catches the bug well, but its bundled Test 5 makes attribution harder.
